purpose: Three featured success stories side by side: each column is a client's mark on a face painted in the client's own brand colour, over a one-line story that links to the case. With `reveal="hover"` each column is one card instead: the client's reversed logo on its brand face, which opens while hovered or focused to reveal the story line and a "Read story" cue, the whole card linking to the case; below the large breakpoint those cards stack and stay open. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-story-columns-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `module`, `registration-frame` and `logo-wall`. The retired `'customer-spotlight'` `_id` resolves here with `reveal: 'hover'`.
useWhen: Use ClientStoryColumnsSection for three or four client cards in brand colours linking to case studies; `reveal="hover"` shows the story on hover.
avoidWhen: For a bento of client stories with photos and logos → use `client-mosaic-section`.
related: `logo-wall` — the single-mark wall each column's face is rendered with.
bestPractices: Three cells for `reveal="always"` (the grid is three columns from the medium breakpoint); three or four for `reveal="hover"`, which shares the row between them.
With `reveal="hover"` use the client's reversed (white) logo and one sentence per story; `logoWidth` sizes the mark as a share of the card (default `35%`).

Leave `brand` out for a client the client registry knows (`clientBrand(name)` from `@aziontech/ui/assets/client-registry`): the face reads its colours, and its ink, by `name`. Add a missing client to the registry rather than writing its hex colours into the page.

Pass `brand` only for a one-off client the registry does not carry: `base` and `glow` may be any CSS colour, and `ink` is `'dark'` when the face is light enough that the link text must be dark. Left out, the ink is chosen by measured contrast: a hex `base` on which white text would fall under 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) takes dark ink. A cell with neither paints a black face.
